text:
Kevin Stenlund won a Stanley Cup with Florida in 2023-24 as a checking center, and that is still the job in Utah: 13.4 minutes a night and penalty kill work. The offense has gone missing even by those standards. He is pointless in twelve straight games on 3.3 expected points, with 1 goal and 4 assists through 22.

This isn't simply bad luck. His own chances have thinned out over the last ten games, and at five on five the Mammoth have been about six points worse in expected goal share (chance quality) with him on the ice than without him. Evolving-Hockey had a similar view last season: his team created 0.34 fewer expected goals per 60 with him out there, bottom 1% of forwards.

There is some bad luck on top of it. Utah has scored 4.9 fewer goals than the chances deserve with him on the ice, which our numbers expect to even out.

He plays like Jordan Greenway and Oskar Sundqvist: kills penalties, shoots rarely. His value is in the defensive details, and in a losing stretch that's harder to see.
